observations: gsv_control_link_112_2313b6b71a (2020-11, station +1.4 m) is the clearest front-facing view of the far-side mast arm: the arm extends left from a far-right corner pole over the westbound roadway and carries three vehicle heads facing the camera. Leftmost head shows a lit red lamp whose shape (circle vs arrow) is not resolvable; middle head shows a lit green upward arrow (YOLO traffic-light proposal); right head (nearest the pole) shows a lit green upward arrow, any other indications unresolved.

gsv_control_link_112_c28aca3e20 (2020-11, station -9.3 m) shows the same far-side mast arm and heads at smaller size (YOLO box = leftmost head), plus a near-right corner pole whose mast arm runs diagonally away from the camera; heads on that near arm and on the near-right pole are seen side-on or from behind, so their faces cannot be read and they likely face a crossing road.

In c28aca3e20 a small pedestrian-style head with a red/orange lit display stands on the right sidewalk beyond the near-right pole; symbol not resolvable. A white sign is cut off at the right frame edge near the bottom of the near-right pole; unreadable.

In 2313b6b71a a small red/orange diamond-like sign (the YOLO 'stop sign' proposal) stands on the far right sidewalk beyond the crosswalk; its shape and text are not resolvable and it may not be a stop sign. A white sign with a dark arrow-like symbol stands in the planted median on the left beyond the crosswalk; symbol and facing unclear.
A thin horizontal object on a vertical stalk above the far mast arm in 2313b6b71a is seen edge-on (possibly a sign blade or luminaire); not readable.
No lane-use arrow signs or turn-restriction text facing the westbound approach are readable at this resolution.

detail_requests.question: Leftmost head on the far-side mast arm: is the lit red indication a circular ball or a left-turn arrow, and what are the unlit lens symbols?
Head nearest the far-right pole: confirm the green arrow direction(s) and check for any additional arrow or sign mounted beside it.
Red/orange sign on the far right sidewalk (YOLO stop-sign proposal): shape, text, and whether it faces the westbound approach.
White sign in the left median beyond the crosswalk: read its symbol/text (keep-right, one-way, turn restriction?) and its facing.
